utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-99-36-PT, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hoping that calling the case is not the only thing that we'll be able to accomplish today. Yes, General Talic, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I do hear you in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, General Talic. You may sit down. Mr. Brdjanin. Good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I can hear you in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Joanna Korner assisted by Susan Grogan, case manager. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you. Appearances for Radislav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I'm John Ackerman and I am here with Tania Radosavljevic and Marela Jevtovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I Thank you. Good morning to you. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. I'm Natasha Ivanovic-Faveau, assisted by Fabien Masson. I represent General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before I ask you whether there are any preliminaries, let me give you some news which can be bad or good depending on who is the recipient. This morning this courtroom is needed for the Initial Appearance of one of the newcomers. That will be at 10.30, which means that we will need to vacate this courtroom at 10.00, at the latest, which also means that we will not be able to resume until at least after 10 minutes after Judge Schomburg would have finished with the Initial Appearance. I'm sorry I couldn't give you any forewarning on this. I was only informed this morning, although someone did leave a message on my voice mail at 6.00 or 6.30 yesterday evening, when I had already left. So that's the position. So, Madame Fauveau, I would imagine you will be prepared in case you're not in a position to finish your cross-examination today, you will need to continue it on Tuesday, when we resume. Mr. Ackerman, you'll certainly not be in a position to start today for sure. So that's the situation. Having said that, if there are any preliminaries, and I see the three of you on your feet, any preliminaries? No. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the exhibit -- I'm sorry - the witness list is being copied at the moment, but I'll deal with that later. There are some slight wrinkles. There are certainly changes from the list that Your Honour had because of the two witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what you gave me to understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right. But I'll deal with that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was aware that Judge Schomburg was doing the first appearance, but somehow or other I thought he might be prepared to do it in court 2, as there was only one defendant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that doesn't allow for an audience.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Very true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: An Initial Appearance sometimes does appeal for -- to an audience anyway. But it's something that has been already agreed upon. Yes. Judge, good morning to you. Ms. Korner has got a few more questions to you, after which Madame Fauveau, representing General Talic, will commence her cross-examination, which presumably I assume it will not be concluded today. There will be arrangements made for you to return to this Tribunal, unless he's going to stay here. I don't know what the arrangements are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm almost certain he'll be staying here, Your Honour. I doubt they will fly him back for the four days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, you will be required to attend again, Judge, and Tuesday, and presumably then by Wednesday at the latest Thursday you'll be free to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I'm working on the basis we've got the next witness lined up for Tuesday. Almost certain he'll finish on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Monday is off.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Holiday

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I wouldn't be confident that he will finish on Tuesday, if I were Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. Good morning. Yes, Madame Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just wanted to inform you that I don't think that I will finish today. I think that I will finish my cross-examination on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The impression that I got from you yesterday also indirectly through Mr. Ackerman was that you would be taking the whole session. So, Judge --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just mention something? Because now I've done it, Your Honour, may I just mention something. Having said I never call you Judge because of the Judge business. I did ask for indications, and I understood perfectly that Madame Fauveau would be taking a full session. I understood, however, Mr. Ackerman, that he would not be of any length of time with this witness, in fact, he would be quite short, because we had this discussion last week. I'm only raising it for this reason: We're getting a series of complaints from the VWS about the length of time witnesses have been kept here. Most of it I agree. These have been very lengthy witnesses from the point of view of the Prosecution. But it would be helpful if an indication, a realistic indication, could be given of how long cross-examination is going to take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem is that had we gone on regularly, I mean, as planned, as scheduled, in other words, today, Madame Fauveau would have finished her cross-examination. Then, presumably, I mean, out of a whole session, one would have expected Mr. Ackerman, according to what he informed us, to finish well before the end of that session, but if Madame Fauveau is not going to finish her cross-examination today and it is quite obvious she won't be in a position to finish it because we won't have a full session today and Mr. Ackerman not knowing exactly how much of Tuesday's session Madame Fauveau will be using, utilizing, I can't call up on him and tell me whether he will be finishing on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no. I appreciate that. But I'm just asking, I mean, if we can, to get some realistic estimates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usually when Mr. Ackerman says something in this courtroom, it's not far off from what he really means. So I would -- I wouldn't even like to put the question again to him. I mean, I think I can rely on his word, which he's kept throughout so far since we started this trial. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Ms. Korner may not appreciate that a lot of what one does on cross-examination depends upon what one hears during the direct examination, and it's been -- there's been, I think, two or three days of direct examination since I made my last estimate, and I would say that the time I need to spend has probably doubled as a result of what has happened on direct the last couple of days. So, you know, I will take the time that I think I need. I won't use up time. But it seems to me that if the concern is that witnesses are here too long, perhaps Ms. Korner could desist from reading documents to the Court and having the witness confirm that she is reading properly. That would probably shorten things up a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Ms. Korner, I would suggest to you to ignore Mr. Ackerman and proceed with your first question and the next ten documents, more or less, so that we finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm tempted to say something about Mr. Ackerman's the last remark but I won't. I'll resist it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you get a suggestion like that from a Mediterranean take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could Judge Draganovic have the binder back again, please. And if the usher would be kind enough to turn to find the document marked Exhibit P408, which is behind divider 36.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Korner: [Continued].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 6th of August, 1992, which was the day after or around the same day that the reporters went to the Omarska camp, and it deals with -- it's addressed to the 1st Krajina Corps command, headed "Selection of prisoners in the Manjaca POW camp from the Prijedor -- I'm sorry. It's from - I beg your pardon - it's from the 1st Krajina Corps, and it's signed by Colonel Bogojevic and it's addressed to the Prijedor national security sector. It states this: "By processing the war prisoners in the Manjaca POW camp, we realise that a certain quite large number of them, according to incrimination, do not deserve to be treated as prisoners of war. They did not have weapons, they did not participate in combat, they were not in uniform, et cetera. In order to free space to accommodate potential new prisoners in the Manjaca POW camp and in order for each prisoner to get the treatment they deserve, we ask that you send a responsible official, or several of them, to Manjaca who would, together with the security organ at Manjaca, carry out a selection of prisoners who could be released and prisoners who must remain in the camp. This is all in aid of the proposal and the release of that section of the prisoners who do not fall into the prisoner of war category. According to our records, in Manjaca there are currently 944 prisoners from the Sanski Most municipality. As you know, we have recently been attacked by the European and world media in connection with the existence of concentration camps, so this is sufficient reason to carry out a prisoner selection." Two questions, please, Judge: First of all, you told us that the majority of the prisoners who were with you were civilians. Do you recall any releases around August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, these were all civilians, particularly those from Sanski Most and Kljuc, Prijedor. All of these people were civilians. There were no prisoners of war, people who would be in uniforms. And as to the question whether anyone was released, I do know that on one occasion it was said that a group, a smaller group of people from Kljuc, would be released. I think that these people were sick people, elderly people, and that group was called out for two days, and they waited to be released. At one point they were even taken out of the internal part of the camp where the command is. But on both days they came back and they never in fact left. A small group from Sanski Most, if I'm not mistaken, I think they were released. These were under-age people and elderly people. But there may have been around 80 people, or maybe even less. I know, for instance, Mohamed Arapovic, a neighbour of mine. He was released. A boy by the name of Mujagic was released. So I do remember that. It may have been in that time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Korner. Judge, I forgot this morning to ask you to make the solemn declaration. Could you just make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And next question is -- comes from me. On the basis of the solemn declaration that you have just made, could you kindly confirm that the answer you gave to Ms. Korner's question a few minutes ago is the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sit down and we can continue. Thank you. Sorry, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's a slight side track, but I've never quite understood why witnesses already bound by the oath should have to take it everybody morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I'm used to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move, then, simply to note that the next exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment again. In the B/C/S version of this document --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's stamped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's stamped, but the left before the text as such begins after the word "selekcija," there is a word "ratnih."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't know where Your Honour is looking at at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you look at the English version, fifth line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Selection of -- and there is a black redacted part of the text or whatever it is. In the Serbo-Croat version, the word which has been redacted in English is visible. You can read it, ratnih. What does that mean, Judge? If he can ...

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the word "ratnih"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I know you're asking me to tell me what it means, but the idea is that the interpreters will translate to me the word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Selection of prisoners of war in the Manjaca prisoner of war camp. That means that we were treated as prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The word which has been cancelled is "war." What is the word for "war" in your language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we just move very quickly to the next document in the bundle, marked P714, simply to note -- it apparently deals with -- it's an SDS invitation to attend a meeting, and we'll see -- to include a report on General Talic's visit. The next divider, 37, and I think that's a document you personally -- no, maybe it's not this one. It's the next one, I think. Yes. The next document, P715, that, I think, again being a record of the minutes of the executive committee was a document that you handed to a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, and also the following document, neither of which I wish to go through, which is P716.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the next document, P717, behind divider 40, I think we simply need to note that this is a report concerning collection centres, as described, and the actual report, it deals with a number of municipalities, but the report -- and there's a completion of -- I'm sorry. It was signed by each of the heads of the local SJBs and Sanski Most appears in that report at page 6 of the translation onwards. And Mr. Ackerman needn't worry I'm not proposing to read through that. It's there. And it's a document that comes up in all the municipalities virtually, Your Honours, so we can look at it. Could we move, then, to Exhibit 718, which is behind divider 41. And again, that's a document that you handed personally to a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. P719, the same. And then if we move -- and P721, which is behind divider 44. And again, I don't propose to go through those, Your Honour. Can we move now, please, to P725, which you will find behind divider 48. Now, this is a document, I think, Judge, that you personally handed to a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's apparently - and I want to look at this - some sort of letter dated the 16th of September, 1992 and signed by the -- what's called the intervention Platoon, SOS. And there are three signatures, if one looks at the original. And unless I'm mistaken, it's the same stamp that we saw earlier from the SOS announcement. It's not a very good copy, I'm afraid. Can you tell us where you found that? Can you remember where it came from?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was found in the premises of the Sanski Most SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's headed "Report on the work and activities of the SOS, acting as an Intervention Platoon within the 6th Krajina Brigade between the 1st of May, 1991, and the 16th of September, 1992," and it's addressed to fellow Serbs, patriots, gentlemen. And I'm not going to read the first bit. It's apparently - and I'm summarising - a complaint about the way they're being portrayed. Could we turn to page 2, and if you could find in the B/C/S version, please, Judge, the paragraph that begins: "These young men ...": "These young men, I'm thinking of the seven lads who tirelessly brought weapons from the various warehouses and points and armed the Serbian people, risking that the weapons fall into the hands of Ustashas and Green Berets, especially on the routes of Sanski Most to Knin, Sanski Most to Bosanski Petrovac, Sanski Most to Banja Luka, and they did all that while Alija's Muslim police was patrolling and the Serbs were leaving the area at the time." And then it goes on to glorify them. And then the last sentence: "The citizens of Sanski Most know very well that as genuine members of the SDS democratic party, we invested our own funds at the time in order to secure peace. We never allowed large gatherings of SDA and HDZ to take place at any stage, and we broke up any such gathering in the usual way. The SDS from Sanski Most is our witness that we put them into power. It is unbearable to think what could have happened if we had not acted in this way. Blowing up buildings was not in anyone's interest, but we could not crush the Ustashas and Green Berets any other way. No one should take credit for the capture of SDA and HDZ leaders owner the SOS and in part the Serbian police for its action. We were then congratulated and highly praised for it because you need heart to face up to a sniper's barrel and the ones who did not -- who did know who they are." Literally, can you just answer this question, please, yes or no: You've told us about the activities of the SOS. Here they suggest that they were breaking up party gatherings of the SDA and the HDZ. Were you aware that this is what they were doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then just a few more parts of this lengthy document, complaint that the Serbs never mention the name of these lads and then: "Do not forget, these lads never refused a single position in the 6th Krajina Brigade." Then it goes on again that: "Members of the SOS have various other professions." And in the next paragraph: "Because of those who don't want good to come to the Serbian people, I must tell you some more truths. The members are -- ultimatum to the joint authorities especially to the Serbian part of the authorities, to speed things up and take more concrete action in order to create a true government for the Serbian people. Remember the meeting we had on the premises of the Serbian orthodox church, where we particularly warned about the slow implementation of the conclusions reached by the BH SDS and Bosnian Krajina, where we openly identified certain Serbs and their private interests, calling them traitors and accusing them of being hand in glove with the SDA and HDZ for personal profit and to further their careers." And again, do you recall -- was there any public accusation being made by members of the SOS against Serbs who they described as traitors, that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, if we go to the next page, page 4, and if you could find the paragraph that begins: "The attack on the municipality ..." Do you have that, Judge? It says: "I continue chronologically," and then the paragraph begins: "The attack on the municipality ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's on page 5 in the B/C/S, last --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll continue in chronological order. The attack against the municipality. I have found this. It is on page 5 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. "The attack on the municipality of the 30th SOS only carried out the will of the people, who wanted to stop the uncontrolled fascism. That's what it should be called - of the heated extremists from the SDA and the HDZ, in an underhand way and using blackmailing methods, they occupied the municipal building to carry out their dark goals. 45 young men, soldiers with the support of the 5th section of the 4th Battalion embarked on this courageous feat without spilling any blood, and that's how we resolved the question of government in the municipality was solved." "Colonel --" I think that should be Anicic, "could give us more details about it and I'm sure that he wrote it down somewhere. We must also mention how we resolved the previous problem of the SDK, the Serbian tricolour flag started fluttering on top of their buildings and that was that. There you go, gentlemen. Organise your government. We must not forget a little episode," et cetera, et cetera. And then at the top of the page: "After that, one combat action followed another, mopping up Trnovo, Mahala, Hrustovo, Populja [phoen] twice, Marino caught seven extremist Ustashas in the corridor, constant patrols, mopping up, and so on and so forth." Yes. Thank you. If we leave that document, please. Could we just note again that the next document, P726, was, I think, again handed by you to an Office of the Prosecutor, a CSB document. Could we go now, please, to Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P728, behind divider 51. This again was a document I think you handed to the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you remember where you found this, or where it was found?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was found in the premises of the municipal staff, the municipal headquarters of the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a report from the civilian protection staff. Could you find the bit that's headed "A" in the town? That's found in the third page of the translation and is, I think, on the second page of the original B/C/S. The report is from July to October 1992. And there's a sentence that reads in that paragraph "in the town": "Simultaneously with these activities" that's all the clearing activities "a considerable amount of time was spent removal the debris from the town mosque. These activities are still underway and the exhumation and dislocation of the cemetery next to the town mosque will begin after the adoption of appropriate decisions in the Municipal Assembly." Is that cemetery the same as the one you were talking about, the Grede cemetery, or is that a different one?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town mosque in Sanski Most, Hasanbegova mosque was destroyed. It's in the centre of town. At the beginning of the Mahala neighbourhood. And after it had been destroyed, it was an old town area which was 300 or 400 years old. It was an old town cemetery, and it was removed and a parking lot was constructed there. So when we returned there in 1995, in October, it had been completely cleared. It was a completely cleared parking area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the bodies or the coffins that were removed? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how old was that cemetery? How long had it been there?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that. Between 300 and 400 years. It was as old as the town of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, next there's a mention of a place called -- what's the -- can you tell us what the place under "B" is? Could you just tell us what the name of the places the next immediately after that. There's a place that's mentioned. I just can't pronounce it. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pobrijezje. It's a neighbourhood near the town as you go from the centre of the town towards Prijedor, along the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Just see if I can find the big map. Can we just, for a moment --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the map of the area, Your Honour. While that's being done, we'll have a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a reference there to a mosque also debris from a demolished mosque. Before this, what was the ethnic make-up of this village?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The population in Pobrijezje was mainly Muslim, but before the war and now. There are several houses belonging to people of Serbian ethnicity. Below the Pobrijezje neighbourhood, towards Podlug. Podlug is a Serbian settlement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then is Stari Majdan, again they say that they started clearing and removing debris from a demolished religious building, and then there would be sanitation of residential building. Stari Majdan I think is an actual part of Sanski Most; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stari Majdan is an old neighbourhood, an urbanised neighbourhood, which is six kilometres from Sanski Most, in the direction of Ljubija. The majority of the population is Bosniak in this settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can see in fact on the ordinary Sanski Most map Pobrijezje is marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I was going to tell you forget the map, because we have already been --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mosque in Stari Majdan was also destroyed, and this was the clearing out of the religious building of the mosque itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we -- I'm not going to trouble with the rest of this document? Can we move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Ms. Korner, looking at this document, the English version, it starts exactly and continues as in the Serbo-Croat, except that while the English version after page 7 continues then with what seems to be a summary of what is contained in the previous seven pages, that summary does not appear in the Serbo-Croat version, at least the one I have. I have five pages, and that's it, of Serbo-Croat. That excludes the title page. And it seems that the summary of the report has a reference number, which is SM-65/20. It doesn't show up in the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll do a check on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Just for the record, because I don't think it's going to make any difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, but we'll do a check. It may be we've missed some of the pages in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we move, please, briefly, to the next document, Exhibit P729, and this is a report from the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka. It's the SNB, which is the national security department, and it records that apparently by October 1992 there was a radical party operating, and it's purely to note that Mr. Delic, Tomo Delic, was the main initiator. And at the bottom of the page, it states that: "About 20.000 Muslims have moved out of this region, and the remaining 10.000 or so wish to do the same. Muslims have been moving out of this region mostly because of its uncertain future and lack of safety." Then, please, could we move now to document P730, which you will find behind divider 3. We're now going back to the beginning in the numbering. Again, this deals with destruction of religious property. It's a report from the military police, dated the 2nd of November. It's dated on the 1st or the 2nd of November 1992 as printed, unidentified persons attacked the village of Sehovci. On this occasion a mosque in the village was demolished. The attack by identified persons was carried out at around 2145. A strong explosion resounded, the mosque destroyed while the windows of some homes were shattered. On the basis of several interviews conducted, it is apparent that the unidentified persons arrived in a truck and two small cars. The explosive for the mosque which was destroyed was most probably transported from a truck," and so on and so forth. This particular village, how far was that from Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I left the map behind in my room, but I'll check that later.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Sehovci is about two kilometres from the town. The population there is Bosniak, and as far as the destruction of the mosque is concerned, I can say the following: The first house next to the mosque belonged to my sister. I received information concerning the destruction of this mosque from my sister's family. The mosque was shelled and explosives were planted to destroy it. It was shelled from the Serbian settlement of Podlug, and the explosives were planted. It was known that evening that the mosque was going to be destroyed. The inhabitants who lived near the mosque were told to move away. A special military vehicle arrived which belonged to the engineers. And that's how the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is in fact also marked on the little map. One can see it heading in the direction of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is all about -- the next series of documents seem to refer to this village. If you go, please, to the next document, Exhibit P732. This is a Municipal Assembly meeting, and the first item on the agenda which was discussed was -- well, the agenda says: "Report and explanation in connection with the armed operation carried out at Trnovo and Sehovci" and the discussion concluded that a report should be requested from the command of the 6th Krajina Brigade and the public security station on who took part in organising the armed attack on these two places and what the aim of such a large-scale attack was." And then under agenda two, the conclusion being reached was that: "The perpetrators of this heinous crime must be discovered with all speed and the severest measures provided by law must be taken against them." And that deals, as we can look, and I think we've already covered that, the killings of Croats in Kruhare and Skelica. We discovered that with the letter from traitors.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Skelica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just very briefly, from your investigations, who was involved, as you understood it, in this attack on Trnovo and Sehovci?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the 6th Krajina Brigade and the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could we then move -- perhaps the last document and then -- to P733, which can be found behind divider - I'm sorry - divider 8. This is a document I think again that you personally handed to the Office of the Prosecutor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a meeting again of the executive committee of the Sanski Most municipal --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The executive board. Executive board? Okay. It says -- in the translation it says "executive committee." Is that -- is there a difference?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The executive committee is an organ of the Municipal Assembly. The executive committee -- so it's an organ of the Municipal Assembly, and the executive committee is an executive organ of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I hope this isn't going to matter, Your Honour, because I don't want to pursue this. If it does matter, then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Conclusions. 2: "Arrange a visit to the 1st Krajina Corps command and inform the Corps commander of the situation in the municipality and the issue of reducing the number of battalions in the 6th Krajina Brigade to 4, and it was going to be asked to analyse its work. And then over the page, item 9 states that: "The political and security situation in Sanski Most, a report by the public security -- it must be "station" and the brigade command and a report from a meeting of the 1st Krajina Corps commander General Talic shall be included in item 1." And then finally, before we have to break, P735, which is behind divider 10, simply, I think, to note that the -- this is a document again that you handed directly to the Office of the Prosecutor, and the decision that was reached was that the command of the 6th Krajina Brigade and the public security station are requested to submit a report on who participated in the organisation of the armed attack on Trnovo and Sehovci. I think this is, in fact, just a repetition of what we've seen already.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, and just to note, please, P736. You handed this, I think, directly to the Office of the Prosecutor. It's a document - and I simply want to know where you got it from - it's a document addressed -- I'm sorry - headed "Why did the intervention against the Serbian people start?" Signed by somebody called Professor Buscovenovic [phoen], and it seemed to be some sort of --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. Behind which divider is this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Divider 12. You're not getting translation?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I found it in the premises of the Municipal Assembly in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's some kind of polemic, address, it looks like, to the European community. Yes. Because if one looks at the top of page 2, you people of the European community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would be more interested in knowing who this Professor Buscovenovic is and whether he held any position of power or influence at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was found in the office of the then president of the municipality, Nenad Koraslin [phoen]. It's some sort of a report, some sort of essay. Maybe Mr. Brdjanin knows who Buscovenovic is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Leave Mr. Brdjanin alone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know, is the answer. All right.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And with that I --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- We can stop for the time being. We break until necessary. I can't tell you when we are going to start again. It depends on --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was told that the appearance wasn't in fact until 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but we need to vacate the room half an hour before because they have to change the tapes and do this and that and when it's all over, they need another ten minutes to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can someone notify us in the Defence room when we should come back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could someone notify us in the Defence room when we should return?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to give instruction to Madam Chuqing Chen now to do precisely that. Not just you, but also Ms. Korner and ourselves. We'll resume just after 10 minutes following the end of the Initial Appearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I can say is this month is jinxed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while I just find my place again. I'm sorry. We've just come back into court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madame Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to apologise on behalf of Fabien Masson, who is downstairs and making photocopies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Everything is being reorganised. Can I hand out the list now of the witnesses for the next -- or the revamped order of witnesses. I haven't had an opportunity to give it to the Defence yet, so -- and to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just very quickly point out: There's one major difference, and that is the second witness from the humanitarian organisation will not be testifying at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He was going to testify 29th and 30th of this month, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It was effectively a week on Monday or Tuesday. We've got another holiday, haven't we, somewhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he will not be for various administrative reasons. So what we've done is moved the witnesses up. What we've done is when we checked the list yesterday after Your Honour raised it Witnesses 139 and 143, who were the ones who were difficult, they have been moved back. And so the next witness, starting, I hope, possibly on Tuesday, probably on Wednesday, will be 7.29 and will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She is trying to provoke you again, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we'll give Your Honours the statements at the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. Thank you. So I take it that the next witness will be 7.29.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He is not protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We won't mention his name because he might ask for protection between now and Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly. Although I think it's unlikely.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madame Faveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we be told about the witness who is not coming from this organisation? I think it is witness 723.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 7. -- Yes, exactly. 7. --

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is he not going to come at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He is coming, but not at the stage that we anticipated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that this is the witness that some time back you had warned us that if we don't really get him on the date -- on the day that he had asked for, it will be at least six months before he will turn up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right. Not six. It will be at least four, Your Honour. It won't be before September at the earliest. But for various reasons we've had to make that alteration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm told I had just dealt with document 736. I'm trying to find it on my own list. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. If we look please at document -- the next document P737, at the divider 13. Somebody has taken the bundle away from the witness. Again, this is a document I think that you personally submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that right, Judge?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it shows the allocation of what's described as the allotment of apartments for temporary use. Just very quickly: These -- the former tenants, were they of mixed ethnicity, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. Does this refer -- are you referring to the same document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You've been given -- I'm sorry. It's the second divider, number 13, and somebody has directed you to the first divider. It's just the first page. In fact, Judge, other than the fact that you gave it, unless you know who these people were, it's perhaps better not to guess at ethnicity. It's my fault.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That you gave this document to the Office of the Prosecutor. Right. Okay. Can we move, then, please, to the document at the next page -- the next divider, that's number 14, document P738. And I just want to confirm with you again, when you look at it, that this was a document you personally handed to a member of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we just look at page 3 for a moment, our page 3, just before we get to item 2, it's your page 6, I believe, in the B/C/S. No. Maybe not. There's lots of double ones. Sorry. No. It's -- it says "to request the command of the 6th Krajina Brigade to intensify political work in the battalions." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then can we move, please, now quickly on to P742, which you will find behind divider number 18. This is dated the 15th of December, 1992 and is a document headed, "War bulletin of the 6th Krajina Brigade" and is apparently dealing with the fact that Colonel Basara was leaving, and a Colonel Kajtez had been appointed. Could you go to the end of the document, because there's a paragraph that says: "Under the command of Colonel Branko Basara, the 6th Krajina Light Infantry Brigade took part in the following actions: The liberation of Bosanska Krupa, the liberation and cleansing of Hambarine, Kozarusa, and Kozarac, a creation of conditions for the takeover of Kljuc, the seizure of weapons throughout the municipality, the military victory against the Muslim extremists in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo. The brigade took part in the cleansing of the entire territory on the left bank of the Una River and the cleansing of Sanica, Krasulja, Hrustovo, Vrhpolje and then in carrying out tasks in the valleys of Bosna and Vrbas, and the breakthrough and the safeguard of the corridor." The map that you found in the 6th Krajina Brigade showing the movements, did that correspond with what's written here, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does correspond to it completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then if we could move, please, to the next document that I wanted to ask about, P744, which is behind divider 20. This again, I think, is a document that you yourself recovered and handed to the Office of the Prosecutor, and it deals with the disposal of both rubbish and people and animals, it looks like. It's a long list of what happened. Do you remember where this document came from?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I found this document in the communal organisation in the socially owned organisation Sana in Sanski Most. Public utilities organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I was go to ask. And if we just look at one example, we can see on the 9th of June, page 3 of our translation, item number 26, burial of 35 people killed. It doesn't say where. In the next entry for the 10th of June, burial of two persons killed, visit Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I note, again, I mean, the English version stops at number 309; the B/C/S one continues from 310 and you have one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, thirteen pages times 2, 26, including extensive notes which are not translated into English language. Do I take it these are irrelevant and you are not tendering them into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The whole document was put in, but the only part that was thought to be specifically relevant was the part up to December 1992 because that's when the indictment period ends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's the reason?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll try and save the Translation Unit some effort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I just wanted -- I imagined there would be an explanation, but I just wanted to hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we go to the next exhibit, please, 746, which is behind divider 22. And what happened, I think, is we don't seem to have the whole document, and so it starts in the middle of -- we start the original B/C/S version starts at page 5 of the document, and so the translation begins at that part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It appears to be some kind of history of the 6th Krajina Brigade again. And can we turn to page 4 in the translation. And it's the paragraph beginning: "On the basis of information ..." And I'm afraid I cannot help as to where that paragraph starts. I would think at the bottom of the -- page 8 in the original version, somewhere there. There's a paragraph beginning: "On the basis of information gathered by the Sanski Most Public Security Service ..." Yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of information gathered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, here we see in that paragraph "gathered by the Sanski Most public Security Service, the Banja Luka CSB," and so on. "The intentions of the Muslims and the SDA were uncovered and measures taken to expose and arrest the planners of a heinous massacre of the Serbian people. The Muslims and the Croats were politically and militarily organised through the territory of Sanski Most municipality in their local communities, where they had set up detachments," et cetera. As far as you were aware, Judge, was there any planning by you or anyone that you knew of a massacre of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It carries on to talk about the units being part of the Bihac Cazin Territorial Defence. You had about 2.000 armed men and intended to arm a further 4.000. Arms from SDA leaders, who obtained them through various channels. The best organised and most inveterate extremists were the Muslims in Vrhpolje, Hrustovo, Mahala, and Trnovo. The principal leaders and ideologists in all Muslim villages were the imams and SDA leaders." And then this: "Following a director from Sarajevo and organised by Durakovic's SDP party, they set up a peace movement, the so-called Peace League. The aim of this movement was to put the brigade and the Serbian people out of action so that they could gain time and additionally arm and equip their forces and then set out against the Serbs, take power by military means, and establish control over the territory. In the Peace League, the chief activists were the wealthiest and most renowned Muslims whom the Serbs had trusted to a certain extent until then." Now, you told us, Judge, that you were a member of this peace movement. Was the aim of this movement to put the brigade and the Serbian people out of action, et cetera, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the Peace League in Sanski Most. The objective of the Peace League was to ensure that the citizens gained trust, trusted each other, to make it possible for them to live together and to help them organise against the warmongerers, et cetera. That was the league's main objective. And the Peace League was a multi-ethnic organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then finally this: The documents found show that they intended to commit genocide against the Serbian people, kill them, expel them, and create a Muslim state in these parts. All renowned Serbs and their families were to be killed and hanged in the park in Sanski Most. Serbian girls and women were to be put in brothels to bear offspring to the Mujahedin and janissary. Sharia laws and government were to be introduced as in Iran. Male Serbian children were to be circumcised and brought up according to Islamic laws and principles." Was that what your aim was?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absurd. This is horrible propaganda. This was published in the media at the beginning of the aggression against Sanski Most. This was broadcast over the Serbian radio, and when the inspectors interrogated the prisoners, or rather, the imprisoned citizens, they spoke about this kind of stupidity. This is the worst kind of stupidity. This was done by those who felt the hatred, those who wanted blood and war and who encouraged people to go to war. This is fascist ideology. This is shameful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the pamphlet or whatever it is goes on to talk about your designs being foiled by the arrival of the brigade and then again describes the various operations. Could we now, please, go then to just to note again the next document, P747, at divider 23, was a document submitted by you to the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document, please, P748, at the next divider, at number 24. This document is a conclusion of the assembly, within the Crisis Staff or war staff seems to have gone. It signed by Rasula, 26th of February, 1993, the decision on the exhumation of remains in the cemetery in the town's centre beside the mosque and the cemetery in Zdena is hereby adopted and must include an exhumation in the cemetery near the public utility enterprise." I think you told us already about the cemetery in the town's centre. The cemetery in Zdena, where was that?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zdena. It's a neighbourhood. It's a part of the town. It's about approximate one and a half kilometres away from the town centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that -- yes. I think again we can see that on the map marked in the direction of Bosanska Krupa. Was that a Muslim cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a Muslim cemetery, and also the one near the public utility enterprise. These are all Muslims cemeteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want for the record to object to this and any subsequent documents, because I think from now on they're all outside the period of the indictment, and I frankly don't think they shed light on anyone's state of mind which would make them admissible at all. They're talking about specific events that can't possibly be charged in the indictment because they're outside the period of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but, Mr. Ackerman, I only partly see your point, because we're talking of an order or a decision on the exhumation of remains, dated 26th February 1993. Presumably, as I take it, we're talking of persons that died earlier and were buried, and therefore we need to establish further what this is all about, to see whether it's relevant or not. If we're talking of persons who died or were killed or whatever outside of the period we're talking about, yes, you're right. But more or less, I mean, I find this document here as one which calls for some explanation. Why would Nedeljko Rasula, president of the Municipal Assembly of Sanski Most, on the 26th of February, 1993, proclaim this decision?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it refers back to also an earlier decision within 1992 in respect of the cemetery in the town centre, where there was an order given that it should be -- or there's a -- I'm just trying to remember which document it was - that the remains -- the cemetery should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of -- why would an allegedly Serb president of the Municipal Assembly in 1993 order the exhumation of corpses from -- I mean, there must be a reason. I mean, I can't speculate on what the reason is, so please --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I will ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned to Sanski Most --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That maybe will provide you, Mr. Ackerman, with an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, can I deal with it this way: When you returned to Sanski Most in 1995, you've already told us what happened to the town centre cemetery. What had happened to the other two cemeteries that are mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two other cemeteries had also been desecrated. The goal was to remove any evidence, any trace, of the Islamic faith and culture. So the old cemeteries had to be removed. And since they did a new zoning plan, the land was to be used for some buildings. I think that we had a decision of the Crisis Staff yesterday. I remember that the Mahala area was already foreseen for the construction of some buildings. They changed the names of the neighbourhoods or of the parts of the town. The goal was to remove anything that would be reminiscent of Bosniaks, Muslims, of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because they said that that had to be a Serbian town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you still object to the document, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Your Honour was presuming that it had something to do with persons who may have been killed during the war, and it was an exhumation of those.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was just asking for a clarification, because it obviously begs the question that the municipal assembly is deciding for the exhumation of three cemeteries. It doesn't say some remains; exhumation of remains. So presumably it's the exhumation of everything that is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it falls -- if there's any offence here at all, it falls under desecration of religious facilities, and it's in 1993, and that would not be within the indictment. These are graves that the witness has told us are maybe as much as 300 years old, and so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me ask one question to the Witness. In your opinion, Judge, was this decision by way of implementation of the previous decision of the Crisis Staff that you referred to earlier and which was shown to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I wanted to confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed, Ms. Korner, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we now move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I take it, Your Honour that my objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Implicitly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we move, then, and there are only two more documents, P749, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, I think, Judge, this is a document that you personally handed to a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor in 1996.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you found it, or where it was found?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security station in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the document consists of a certificate in respect of this gentleman Mile Strbac, I hope, and then a statement, or a record of an interview with this man on the 22nd of March, 1993. And it regards his involvement in the planting of explosives in houses belonging to non-Serbs in the various areas. Can you tell us: Are these areas that are mentioned - Husinovci, Donji and Gornji Kamengrad? Are they in the Sanski Most municipality?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. If you look at the dates, it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want a clarification from Mr. Ackerman, because since before he said this document and others which will be following, whether you are objecting to this one, 749.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's clear, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I better say something about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It refers to 1992, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but if you can avoid the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Other than an objection that may have been made at the beginning of the case, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look briefly at the contents of this interview with this man, who was a policeman, apparently, and he talked about involvement in planting of explosives. He says his involvement in the plan began in March 1992, when he went to Knin to train in handling explosive devices, and he names the people who went with him. And then underlined in the translation, as indeed in the original: "I was told that the training was being carried out on the orders of the Sanski Most SDS, whose party activists from Suhaca sent us on the course. When the course finished, we came to Sanski Most to start planting explosives in houses and buildings owned mainly by Muslims and, more precisely, their leaders and extremists." And then he asked why he was being interviewed like this. And he says, at the bottom: "What I shall say, I say to you personally, but will not confirm it anywhere, because I believe that I have done nothing wrong, nothing for which I should bear responsibility. My activities were all under the auspices of the SDS and, later, the 6th Krajina Brigade." Then: "Before I joined the reserve police force I was involved and active in the case of the mining of somebody called Hasib Kamber's vehicle in the Narodni front suburb. A herbal remedy shop belonging to Dr. Dervis Cavic [phoen], again in the same place, and a pastry shop. The doctor, is that the doctor that was in Manjaca with you that you spoke about? You have to say yes.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Hasib Kamber was the secretary of the SDA party and he was killed. He was in prison and then he was killed and his body was found in the mass grave in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of these activities against these people that he refers to? Did you hear about them at the time?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an investigating judge, I attended the on-site investigations in these cases, unfortunately, and I was able to see with my own eyes that this was indeed the case. Such explosions at that time, there were 44 such explosions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he talks about mining houses and the mosque and the house of various other people, and he mentions other incidents. Then at the end he says: "As for how we got the explosives, I hereby state that they were procured through the army from Korcanica, where they were stored. It was mainly TNT. I also do not wish to mention the people through whom I procured the explosives. I hereby state that the explosives found on us, which were taken from a warehouse called Dolinica, owned by the Kamengrad mine, were not using for mining," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May we return just for a moment, because I've been doing a bit of research here. The document that I originally objected to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that is P748A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Was represented to be, both by the witness and Ms. Korner, and I think inadvertently - I'm not suggesting anything other than that - to be the carrying out of a prior decision by the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In fact, the prior document in that regard was 728, and it was a report from the municipal civilian protection staff. And what it says with regard to that - and it's pretty clear that's what was being referred to - on page 3, "That the exhumation and dislocation of the cemetery next to the town mosque will begin after the adoption of appropriate decisions in the Municipal Assembly." And what we see then next is a decision of the Municipal Assembly which does not take place until 1993, which I again suggest to you puts it clearly outside the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was this the document, Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure it's right. I didn't have an opportunity to go back and check, but in our submission, it makes no odds. Clearly it was in the contemplation of the civil defence unit that that's what was going to be ordered and they got around to ordering it in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman, for your comment, which will be taken in consideration of, together with what Ms. Korner has remarked in regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The paragraph is page -- page 3. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to be clear, it's page 3 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: In the paragraph A in the town, near the end of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I've found it. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then the final document that I would like you to look at, please, Judge, Prosecutor's Exhibit 752, at divider 28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 28th of March, 1994, but refers back to 1992 and talks about the clashes with what are described as Muslim paramilitary formations in Vrhpolje, Hrustovo, Trnovo, Lukavica, and Modranj [phoen]. And then we're back to the question of burial. A number of Muslim extremists who had moved members of their families to other areas before the outbreak of these clashes were killed in this fighting. Because of this, they were buried in common graves by members of their own people, neighbours, and other people employed by the competent organs. Following the cessation of fighting in these areas, some people who took part in burying those killed left our area in convoys on release from the Manjaca camp and in other ways. Their information has been used under the influence of Muslim media propaganda and the media of certain Western countries for propaganda aimed at more successful fighting, increasing international pressure against the Serbian people." Then: "The Muslim papers have quoted specific locations accompanied by comments intended to portray the Serbian people as genocidal. To counter such occurrences and to prevent, in good time, the use of such events for propaganda purposes and pressure on the Serbian people, we believe that it is necessary to suggest that the relevant institutions activate the competent organs in Sanski Most to sanitise the locations in question." Now, Judge, what actually happened? What did that actually mean?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch sent from the State Security Service, its Prijedor detachment. It was sent -- well, this means that the locations mentioned here must be sanitised, in other words, hidden, concealed, removed someplace else. That's what it means. There is a whole series of documents, and also a diary that indicates who actually did that, in operational terms. And I can say to you that all the mass graves and all the individual grave sites of all the victims, Bosniaks and Croats, in the Sanski Most municipality were concealed. But we have managed to find -- identify most of them, although there remains a substantial number that has yet to be uncovered, and we're working on it. These are the victims from 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were all the graves that were found the original burial spots, or were there graves which have been exhumed which appear to be secondary, in other words, the bodies have been removed from the first burial place?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mass grave sites that we exhumed, I think they were not secondary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any graves that were found that were secondary graves, in other words, not the original burial sites? Not mass graves so much, but other graves. If you're not -- say so straight away.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had credible information, reliable information, about some grave sites that I received from some persons who were actually involved in burying the victims, and I did not find these grave sites, which means that the bodies had been moved elsewhere from these sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madame Faveau, I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She understands me anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madame Faveau. I realise that where you're situate is not exactly where you would like to be. Are you comfortable there? In other words, in a situation where you're practically at a line behind the witness, or would you like to change your place?

utterances.speaker: MS. IVANOVIC-FAVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, it doesn't bother me, but perhaps it bothers the witness. If the witness would prefer me to move over there, I can move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, can I ask you to cooperate in this? Because I -- I mean, I was defence counsel myself many years ago, and I think it would be important for the counsel and witness to be able to face each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Or if you prefer, Mr. Ackerman can sit there and you can take this chair over here. Make sure, Madame Faveau, that you have everything in operation and good working order. The microphone is not switched on as yet. Judge, you are going to be cross-examined by Madame Faveau-Ivanovic, who represents the Defence of General Talic. Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. Ivanovic-Faveau:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day.

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you went to Sanski Most on the 15th of October, that you returned there 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you exactly before you returned to Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you decide to return to Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw on television, on CNN or EuroNews, when I saw that Sanski Most was a free town and that it had been placed under the control of the BH army. I saw the forces of the BH army on the square, and I saw them crossing the bridge, and at that point I said, "I'm going to my town now," and I went to my town, and I am still there today, and I'm never going to leave my town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The army of the BH entered Sanski Most on the 10th of October, 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH army entered on the 10th of October. It entered the town in the afternoon or in the evening. That's on the outskirts of the municipality of Sanski Most. I think the BH army had entered the peripheral areas on the 17th of September and that there was fighting that lasted for one month, fighting for Sanski Most. A little under a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did decide to return to Sanski Most when the town of Sanski Most had been liberated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact, you took the decision in five days' time, you packed your bags, and you returned to Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen. I had taken the decision earlier on, the decision to return to Sanski Most, but at that point in time, as soon as I realised that the town was free, I went to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It took you five days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the decision. Well, it took me five seconds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from the time that you found out that Sanski Most had been liberated, up until your return to Sanski Most, five days had passed?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you returned, you carried out exhumations in the Sanski Most area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately. First of all, I searched for graves. I examined graves. I examined documents. I gathered documents. I carried out -- I started with the exhumations a little later. Once certain preparations had been made and once certain graveyards had already been located and once I had informed the International Tribunal and the Office of the Prosecutor in The Hague, when I had been given the agreement of certain organs, their authorisation, once I had made all these preparations, I was then able to start with the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose initiative was it to carry out these investigations?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initiative. Well, listen, I'm, above all, a judge. My official position was that of a judge in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I had been appointed to the municipal court in Sanski Most and I was the president of the Court. Due to my profession, it was my duty to perform such tasks. And secondly, the War Presidency in Sanski Most, or rather, the presidency of the municipality of Sanski Most, assigned me the task of getting involved in this area, that is to say, of investigating -- carrying out investigations into war crimes. And furthermore, in coordination with the cantonal organs, with the judicial organs, the cantonal court, the cantonal prosecution, I established a certain cooperation with these organs and I was given a certain authority, a certain authorisation. So that is basically it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you state when these investigations started?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be precise. Which investigations are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first investigation that you carried out when you returned to Sanski Most. When exactly did this take place, the first investigation which concerned the alleged war crimes?

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen. Sometime around November I started investigating the field -- carrying out investigations in the field to locate mass graves. That was at the beginning of November. But in the second half of October I had already started gathering documents, so I visited all the institutions, all the buildings in which the Serbian authorities had premises, so the Municipal Assembly, the buildings in which the political parties had been, the police station, the public security station. And I went to all the institutions. I then went to certain schools where command -- units had been located, where the Serbian army had been billeted, where their commands were located. I had visited many private houses, many flats. The houses and flats belonged to certain individuals who were important in Serbian politics, who had positions of importance in the commands, in the government.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge --

utterances.speaker: ADIL DRAGANOVIC [Resumed]
